backfill_policy.durable_observed_visibility: effectively absent at historical T, since ingested_at is the backfill instant
backfill_policy.otherwise: stored but inadmissible for strict causal research
backfill_policy.retrospective_visibility: admissible only when source_available_at is determinable, trusted, precision known, and causal quality meets the study's minimum

causal_quality_grades.A: official/primary, exact timestamp, LIVE, strong provenance
causal_quality_grades.B: reliable source, minute precision, trusted timestamp
causal_quality_grades.E: unknown timing or unknown timezone; excluded from strict snapshots

causal_time_policy.durable_available_at_meaning: earliest instant the SYSTEM could durably reproduce the revision
causal_time_policy.ingested_at_monotonicity: ingested_at >= observed_at except when explicitly flagged as a clock anomaly
causal_time_policy.live_observed_available_at_meaning: earliest defensible COLLECTOR knowledge; diagnostic only, never the gate
causal_time_policy.rationale: A collector may observe at 14:00:04 and crash before a durable write that only lands at 14:03. Gating on the observation would let a replay assert knowledge the durable store did not hold at 14:01. Durability is what a replay can honour, so durability gates the snapshot.

three_distinct_notions.ingested_at: instant the normalized revision became durable and therefore replayable
three_distinct_notions.observed_at: instant our collector actually obtained the bytes; under HISTORICAL_BACKFILL this is the instant of the BACKFILL, never a reconstructed historical value
three_distinct_notions.source_available_at: conservative instant at which the SOURCE claims the information became public; null when the source timestamp fails the trust policy

clock_anomaly_policy.effect: diagnostic flag, causal-quality degradation, or fail closed

clustering_policy.as_of_rule: cluster_state(T) uses only observations visible under the mode at T
clustering_policy.canonical_event_id: resolved through lineage as_of(T); never a final cluster identity computed with future observations

lineage.merge: X,Y separate at T1; one event at T2; snapshot T1 unchanged
lineage.split: X single at T1; X1,X2 at T2; snapshot T1 unchanged

D_normalized_commit_failed.retry: new attempt gets a NEW boundary

I_cluster_merge_computed_only.note: no in-memory cluster state is ever used by replay

date_only_policy.rule: a DATE-ONLY source timestamp resolves to the START OF THE NEXT local calendar day in the source timezone, converted to UTC
date_only_policy.why: deterministic; no microsecond debate; a 23h or 25h DST day is resolved by the timezone database rather than by arithmetic; and it never asserts knowledge during the day it cannot place

durability_and_transaction_policy.authoritative_store: the normalized EventStore transaction. A durable raw artefact alone never makes a normalized revision visible; there are not two competing truths.
durability_and_transaction_policy.clock_quality: ingested_at carries a time value but its authority is ordering and durability, not absolute clock accuracy; a clock skew never makes an uncommitted row durable, and source/observed timestamps are never rewritten
durability_and_transaction_policy.commit_order_vs_semantic_order: store commit order may disambiguate STORAGE chronology; it never overrides the equal-source-timestamp conflict rule, and a rowid is never business truth
durability_and_transaction_policy.concurrency_model_v1: a single authoritative SQLite EventStore with serialized write transactions; commit ordering at the store boundary resolves durable ingestion order. No distributed consensus is implied.
durability_and_transaction_policy.distinct_content_race: two distinct revisions may both commit, each with its own durable boundary; normal causal selection applies; no overwrite
durability_and_transaction_policy.durability_honesty: 'durable' means committed under the store's frozen durability configuration - the Phase 1C contract is journal_mode=WAL with synchronous=FULL - not a metaphysical claim about surviving any hardware failure
durability_and_transaction_policy.durable_definition: a normalized EventRevision is durable only after the transaction that makes it visible in the authoritative EventStore has COMMITTED SUCCESSFULLY
durability_and_transaction_policy.failed_commit: no ingested_at; the revision is invisible; no fallback to observed_at
durability_and_transaction_policy.ingested_at: the logical durable-commit boundary associated with the SUCCESSFUL transaction that first makes this immutable revision visible in the authoritative EventStore

ingested_at_assignment.prepared_at: optional diagnostic only; a pre-commit wall clock is never durable evidence and never affects visibility
ingested_at_assignment.rule: the value is assigned inside the transaction but becomes authoritative only if that transaction commits; on rollback or failure it is discarded and never was an ingested_at
ingested_at_assignment.why_not_post_commit_wallclock: stamping after commit would require a second transaction to write it back

durability_and_transaction_policy.lost_acknowledgement_after_success: the already-committed revision is authoritative; deterministic identity and a uniqueness constraint let the retry rediscover and reuse it rather than create a duplicate or a later ingested_at
durability_and_transaction_policy.retry_after_failure: a successful retry receives a NEW durable boundary; a failed attempt never donates its timestamp, even when the content bytes are identical
durability_and_transaction_policy.same_content_race: deterministic identity + uniqueness yields exactly one revision

effective_at_policy.describes: the economic period or instant the event applies to
effective_at_policy.example: July CPI published in August is visible in August, never in July

enrichment_policy.entity_linking: deterministic linking at ingestion may be durable; later relinking is a versioned enrichment, never retroactive
enrichment_policy.late_computed_enrichment: an enrichment computed at 18:00 from a 14:00 article is INVISIBLE to a DURABLE_OBSERVED snapshot at 15:00

entity_identity_policy.fail_closed: an ambiguous mention links to no instrument
entity_identity_policy.linking: every link carries method, confidence and provenance

identifiers.CanonicalEventId: resolved through cluster lineage as_of(T), never a final future-informed identity
identifiers.SourceObservationId: derived from (provider, source_item_id, content_hash); never URL alone

macro_surprise_policy.consensus_requires: its own availability timestamps, provider, revisions
macro_surprise_policy.cutoff_durable_observed: consensus durably available before the release
macro_surprise_policy.cutoff_retrospective: consensus source_available_at before the release, meeting causal quality
macro_surprise_policy.zscore_rule: sigma from prior releases only; current and future releases excluded; insufficient history yields unavailable, never 0

market_context_policy.applies_to_both_event_modes: RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE event snapshots also use a causal market context; retrospective mode never licenses loading final historical prices
market_context_policy.composite_consistency: event and market components each verified exactly under their own causal store at the same declared as_of, with both component identities frozen into the composite identity. No cross-database distributed transaction is claimed or required; determinism comes from identities, not a lock.
market_context_policy.context_window: strictly <= gating availability timestamp AND causally available at T
market_context_policy.corruption: MarketSnapshot corruption, missing required data or ambiguous revision selection makes the composite InformationSnapshot verified replay FAIL CLOSED; no final-history fallback

cumulative_gates.event_time_gate: the bar's economic time must be admissible at T; a bar whose market event time is after T stays forbidden even if a corrupted record claims an earlier ingestion
cumulative_gates.ingestion_gate: the selected revision must be available under Phase 1C declared-ingested as_of(T); a bar whose declared ingested_at is after T is invisible even when its bar time precedes T

market_context_policy.dependency_direction: causal information -> outcome layer, never inverse

derived_market_context.distinction: CAUSAL MARKET INPUT DATA vs DERIVED MARKET FEATURE AVAILABILITY
derived_market_context.input_causality: returns, volatility, volume anomalies, correlation, regime and indicators may be computed ONLY from market rows admitted by the bound market causality policy at T; never from a final full-history dataset
derived_market_context.retrospective_computation: a market feature computed later from inputs that were causally available at T is valid RESEARCH RECONSTRUCTION, but may not be presented as an artefact HyprL held at T unless its own durable availability supports the claim

market_context_policy.final_history_bypass: FORBIDDEN. Reading canonical/final bars filtered only by market timestamp is not a permitted construction of verified causal context.
market_context_policy.future_final_history_mode: if research ever needs FINAL_HISTORICAL_MARKET_DATA it must be a distinct, named, hashed policy, never conflated with causal context. Not created now.
market_context_policy.historical_backfill: a bar whose event time long precedes T but whose declared ingestion is after T is absent from a snapshot at T
market_context_policy.late_correction: a correction ingested after T is invisible at T; the snapshot sees the revision that was selected at T, never the latest or final bar
market_context_policy.live_knowledge_limitation: Phase 1C ingested_at is the DECLARED historical ingestion timeline persisted in the store. It provides replay causality according to that stored timeline. It does NOT by itself prove real-time observation at T - the module's own contract says 'never a live wall-clock, never a promise of lookahead-free real-time knowledge'. The market policy is therefore never labelled LIVE_OBSERVED.
market_context_policy.market_snapshot_as_of: MarketSnapshot.as_of == InformationSnapshot.as_of; never the latest snapshot, the closest one, or one taken after T. A different as_of would have to be bound into identity explicitly.
market_context_policy.phase1c_primitive: the Phase 1C MarketSnapshot builder; market context is CONSUMED from an exact Phase 1C snapshot, never re-derived by this layer
market_context_policy.revision_selection: Phase 1C deterministic selection over declared ingested_at, with contradictory contents at the same maximal ingested_at failing closed rather than being arbitrated by a hash
market_context_policy.storage: separate artefacts joined only by event_id at analysis time

two_protected_directions.A: no post-event market data in causal context (E9)
two_protected_directions.B: no earlier-but-late-ingested market data in causal context (E38)

missingness_policy.durable_requirement: source-health state must itself be durably recorded before it is visible, or replay is impossible
missingness_policy.modelling_caution: outage may correlate with large events; it may be an observable feature but never a zero event count

note: A design contract, not a capture spec. Revision 4 gives market context its own causal barrier: a bar-time filter alone is no longer sufficient, and the market causality policy is bound into snapshot identity.
provider_status: NONE SELECTED; every property REQUIRES WEB VERIFICATION BEFORE FREEZE

raw_first_and_durability_order.rule: a revision observed but never durably persisted never appears in a DURABLE_OBSERVED replay; a surviving raw artefact remains available for forensics and rebuild

raw_integrity_policy.forensic_inspection: if ever offered, must be named NON_VERIFIED / FORENSIC and can never produce a verified InformationSnapshot; V1 preference is fail closed only
raw_integrity_policy.normalized_binds_raw: every normalized EventRevision binds the content hash of the raw artefact it came from

normalized_present_raw_corrupt.why: the snapshot asserts a provenance bound to source bytes that can no longer be verified; a normalized row looking fine is not evidence the bytes behind it were

replay_policy.composite: verified replay reconstructs the event side under its bound causal policy AND the market side under Phase 1C; if either fails the composite fails. No 'causal events + final market data' fallback, and no 'causal market + latest events' fallback.
replay_policy.durable_observed: exactly reconstructible from artefacts durably present by the visibility boundary; a snapshot can never depend on a revision not yet ingested at T
replay_policy.retrospective_source: reconstructible from source artefacts plus the trust policy and causal-quality policy

revision_policy.selection: max(gating timestamp) <= as_of, ties fail closed

snapshot_identity.event_and_market_policies_are_separate: events may be DURABLE_OBSERVED while market data follows PHASE1C_DECLARED_INGESTED_ASOF_V1; the two are distinct causal policies and both are bound. No claim stronger than the weaker evidence.
snapshot_identity.semantics_are_part_of_identity: two snapshots with the same as_of, mode and visible rows but different trust policy versions MUST have different identities

DURABLE_OBSERVED.question: what had HyprL actually observed AND made durable by T

RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE.question: what the world could have known at T according to source timestamps recovered in a backfill

snapshot_read_consistency.forbidden: events read before a concurrent commit while clusters or source-health are read after it
snapshot_read_consistency.precedent: Phase 1C takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE before selection so attested rows cannot move
snapshot_read_consistency.rule: one InformationSnapshot is built from ONE consistent bounded store view; it may never combine causal objects from mutually inconsistent commit states

source_independence_policy.unknown_provenance: independent_source_count is unknown or lower-confidence, never the hostname count

storage_policy.decision: SQLite append-only revision receipts + immutable snapshot manifests, reusing the Phase 1C causal architecture; raw payloads content-addressed as files beside the database

taxonomy_v1.unclassified: GENERAL_NEWS is the fallback, never a silent drop
taxonomy_v1.versioned_reclassification: a V2 taxonomy never rewrites V1 labels; reclassification is a new enrichment revision

timestamp_precision_policy.EXACT_INSTANT: usable at the stated instant; no artificial +1 unit is added when the provider contract guarantees an exact publication instant
timestamp_precision_policy.precision_is_not_semantics: precision=minute does not by itself mean 'published sometime during that minute'; a provider contract may define a truncated display of an exact instant. The trust policy therefore binds precision AND timestamp semantics, and the conservative resolution follows the provider's declared semantics.
timestamp_precision_policy.principle: when a source timestamp identifies an INTERVAL rather than an exact instant, source_available_at is the START OF THE NEXT UNIT in source-local time
timestamp_precision_policy.second_interval: start of the next second, source-local
timestamp_precision_policy.timezone: from the frozen provider contract; DST resolved by the timezone database; unknown timezone yields no source_available_at and never defaults to UTC

timestamp_trust_policy.untrusted_effect: source_available_at = null; only observed_at can bound

verdict_provenance.reevaluation: a V2 never rewrites a V1 verdict; it appends a trust revision
